newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds gain but nervy ahead of credit data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds gain but nervy ahead of credit data.

text.p: Irish government bonds made good gains in active late afternoon trade on Thursday as the market braced itself for the impact of the Irish private sector credit data at 1530 GMT, dealers said.

"Trade has been reasonably busy ahead of the credit figures. A credit rise of about 13.5 percent is already priced into the market, but anything higher will cause ripples. Overall we're steady against gilts and bunds," one dealer said.
At 1450 GMT the eight percent bond due 2001 climbed 18 pence to 103.58 on Wednesday's close to yield 6.84. The eight percent bond due 2006 rose 22 pence to 102.66 to yield 7.47.
"There was a good deal of offshore buying in the morning especially in short paper, but all the day's gains could be wiped off by the credit data," one dealer said.
Most analysts predict the private sector credit level will accelerate by 13.3-13.9 percent but the short end of the market seems to have factored in a higher figure, dealers said.
Earlier the Bank of England boosted the UK money market by annoouncing no change in interest rates despite expectations of a small easing, dealers said.
